song_story.overview: 밤편지, literally 'a night letter,' is a quiet love song written as a message sent across distance in the dark. IU imagines sending a firefly toward someone's window as a stand-in for the words she can't fully say — 'I love you' — while comparing herself to handwriting in sand that the tide is slowly erasing. It's not about conflict or heartbreak so much as the ache of missing someone you can't currently reach, wrapped in the quiet, private ritual of writing at night.
song_story.cultural_root: The song draws on 반딧불 (firefly) as a folk image of a small, fragile light traveling through darkness to reach someone — a classic image in Korean poetry and lullabies for a message sent with love but no guarantee of arrival. The comparison to writing in sand (모래 위에 적힌 글씨) that waves erase reflects a common anxiety in Korean romantic lyrics: love that feels real but impermanent, always at risk of disappearing no matter how sincerely it's expressed.

verse_1.lines: 이 밤 그날의 반딧불을i bam geunarui banditbureul / 당신의 창 가까이 보낼게요dangsinui chang gakkai bonaelgeyo / 사랑한다는 말이에요saranghandaneun marieyo / 나 우리의 첫 입맞춤을 떠올려na uriui cheot immatchumeul tteoollyeo / 그럼 언제든 눈을 감고geureom eonjedeun nuneul gamgo / 가장 먼 곳으로 가요gajang meon goseuro gayo
verse_1.literal: Tonight, I'll send that day's firefly / close to your window / it means 'I love you' / I recall our first kiss / then, whenever you like, close your eyes / and go to the farthest place
verse_1.context: 반딧불 (banditbul) is the firefly, chosen for its small, quiet glow rather than anything dramatic — the message being sent is deliberately modest and gentle, matching a love that doesn't need to announce itself loudly.

verse_2.lines: 난 파도가 머물던nan padoga meomuldeon / 모래 위에 적힌 글씨처럼morae wie jeokin geulssicheoreom / 그대가 멀리 사라져 버릴 것 같아geudaega meolli sarajyeo beoril geot gata / 늘 그리워 그리워neul geuriwo geuriwo / 여기 내 마음속에yeogi nae ma-eumsoge / 모든 말을 다 꺼내어 줄 순 없지만modeun mareul da kkeonae-eo jul sun eopjiman
verse_2.literal: Like writing left on sand / where the waves used to rest / it feels like you'll disappear far away / I miss you, I miss you always
verse_2.context: 파도가 머물던 모래 위에 적힌 글씨처럼 — 'like writing on sand where waves used to stay' — the image works because sand-writing is legible but temporary; she's not afraid he'll stop loving her, she's afraid the connection itself is naturally fragile, like something the tide will eventually take.

chorus.lines: 사랑한다는 말이에요saranghandaneun marieyo / 어떻게 나에게eotteoke na-ege / 그대란 행운이 온 걸까geudaeran haeng-uni on geolkka / 지금 우리 함께 있다면jigeum uri hamkke itdamyeon / 아 얼마나 좋을까요a eolmana joeulkkayo / 난 파도가 머물던nan padoga meomuldeon
chorus.literal: Here inside my heart / I can't take out and give you every word / but it means 'I love you'
chorus.context: 다 꺼내어 줄 순 없지만 — 'I can't take it all out and give it to you, but...' — 꺼내다 (to take out, pull out) treats feelings almost like physical objects stored inside her that she can only partially hand over, which is why the song settles for the one line she can say clearly.

bridge.lines: 모래 위에 적힌 글씨처럼morae wie jeokin geulssicheoreom / 그대가 멀리 사라져 버릴 것 같아geudaega meolli sarajyeo beoril geot gata / 또 그리워 더 그리워tto geuriwo deo geuriwo / 나의 일기장 안에naui ilgijang ane / 모든 말을 다 꺼내어 줄 순 없지만modeun mareul da kkeonae-eo jul sun eopjiman / 사랑한다는 말saranghandaneun mal / 이 밤 그날의 반딧불을i bam geunarui banditbureul / 당신의 창 가까이 띄울게요dangsinui chang gakkai ttuiulgeyo / 좋은 꿈이길 바라요joeun kkumigil barayo
bridge.literal: How did such good fortune / come to me as you? / if we were together right now / ah, how good would that be
bridge.context: 행운 (haeng-un) means good luck or fortune — she frames the relationship itself as something unearned and lucky rather than something she's owed, which fits the song's overall humility and quiet gratitude rather than any dramatic declaration.

artist_context: Through the Night, released in 2017, is one of IU's most enduring ballads and a fixture on Korean 'song for late at night' playlists. Its slow tempo and minimal production put the full weight of the song on her vocal delivery and the lyric's intimacy rather than any big musical hook.
honorific_level: polite — consistent -요/-예요 endings throughout, giving it a gentle, sincere, slightly formal warmth appropriate for a heartfelt letter

grammar_highlights.usage: Polite promise/intention form. Appears in 보낼게요, 띄울게요 — 'I will send' — softly committing to the act of sending the firefly.
Past-retrospective modifier, describing something that used to happen. Appears in 머물던 — 'that used to rest [there],' referring to waves on the sand.
'I can't do X, but...' Appears in 꺼내어 줄 순 없지만 — acknowledging a limit before offering what she can give instead.
